changes.text: HeartGold running natively on Windows, 32 and 64-bit: the DS's own sound driver plays the music, and its 3D is drawn on the PC.
Android: the same 64-bit game as a phone app.
One screen (MENU › ONE SCREEN): every screen of the game drawn again for a single screen; the start menu, every YES/NO, the scripts' choices and the battle's commands as buttons over the picture.
One screen: what the other screen held comes along (an item's description, whose name you're typing, the clock, a place's name), and holding Space shows the other DS screen.
One screen: choosing a starter in Elm's lab shows the Pokémon in a bubble over its ball, with Elm's words.
The D-pad pen: the D-pad moves a pen on the screens you draw on (the signature, the scratch cards, the Alph puzzles, Ball Capsule seals).
Touch buttons: a D-pad, the DS's buttons, the MENU and fast-forward; MENU › TOUCH BUTTONS moves and sizes them and sets the D-pad's kind, how see-through they are and the vibration.
Fast-forward (F, Tab held, or the >> button) at x1.5, x2, x3, x4 or as fast as it goes (MENU › FF SPEED); the music keeps playing and speeds up with it.
Both DS screens, laid out one above the other, side by side, or one big with the other in its corner (F10, MENU › SCREENS).
The DS's wireless over the network: the Union Room with other copies on this PC or the same Wi-Fi, to greet, trade and battle.
Playing online: the Link window (F2) gives an online code to join a friend's game, without opening ports, and keeps a friend list.
The Pokéwalker as a program of its own on Windows: send a Pokémon on a stroll and bring it back with its steps, watts and what it found.
The GBA slot on Windows: Pal Park's migration from a GBA game's save, FireRed for PC's included.
The microphone on Windows: Chatot's Chatter and the hidden microphone test hear the PC's microphone.
Settings, the touch buttons and the friends kept in an .ini next to the save.
The field running very slowly on some phones (4 or 5 frames a second outside, against 25 to 30 in a battle).
MENU › FPS COUNTER › DETAILS: a line under the counter with each frame's work in parts (the game, 3D, 2D, the picture, the sound), to see what makes a phone slow.
